chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) said:
Do not recite anything of the 'azayim (major surahs) in the obligatory prayer, for prostration is an addition to the obligatory prayer.

key_terms.اَلْعَزَائِمِ: Major surahs (specifically Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, An-Nisa, Al-Ma'idah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting major surahs during the obligatory prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines a specific juristic preference (khashf or ikhtiyar) to avoid reciting the major surahs (al-'azayim) during the obligatory prayer, arguing that the physical act of prostration provides sufficient spiritual merit and completion. In Shia scholarly tradition, this reflects the principle that the obligatory components are sufficient for validity, while additional recitations are recommended but not required, preventing unnecessary burden. The ruling highlights the balance between ritual simplicity and the sufficiency of prostration as a key element of worship.
